paper_metadata.title: Glass-Forming Ability, Corrosion Resistance and Mechanical Properties of Zr60-xAl15Ni25TMx (TM = Nb and Ta) Bulk Metallic Glasses

evidence.quote: The thermal stability, glass-forming ability (GFA), corrosion resistance and mechanical properties of Zr 60¹xAl15Ni25TMx (TM = Nb and Ta, x = 0­6) bulk metallic glasses (BMGs) were investigated.

The master ingots with nominal compositions of Zr60¹xAl15Ni25TMx (TM = Nb and Ta, x = 0­6, in atomic percent) were prepared by arc melting of pure metals of Zr, Al, Ni, Nb and Ta with a purity above 99.9 mass % in a purified argon atmosphere.
the rod samples with dimensions of 2 ­22 mm in diameter and 40 mm in length were prepared by copper mold casting.
No distinct sharp diffraction peak can be seen for all patterns except alloy with Ta = 4, which indicates that these alloy rods have a fully glassy structure.

The well-developed shear bands can be seen on the outer surfaces of the tested sample, being consistent with the generation of the plastic flow before final rupture
The vein pattern can be found on the fracture surface of the sample, which indicates the good toughness of BMG

mechanisms.name: atomic size mismatch and efficient atomic packing

evidence.quote: the mismatch of the atomic sizes in Zr­Al­Ni­Nb alloy system can produce an efficiently packed local structure, which facilitates the formation of amorphous phase

the Nb addition into the Zr­Al­Ni alloy cause the generation of strong chemical short-range ordering due to large negative heats of mixing between Al­Nb (¹18 kJ/mol), Ni­Nb (¹30 kJ/mol), Zr­Al (¹44 kJ/mol) and Zr­Ni ( ¹49 kJ/mol) atom pairs
The highly stable Nb-, Zr- and Al-enriched surface film separates the alloy from the corrosive solution effectively.
